'''Ferenc Krausz''' (born 17 May 1962<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=The Nobel Prize in Physics 2023 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2023/krausz/facts/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en-US}}</ref>) is a Hungarian<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-03 |title=Ist Ferenc Krausz ein "österreichischer" Nobelpreisträger? |url=https://www.diepresse.com/17715479/ist-ferenc-krausz-ein-oesterreichischer-nobelpreistraeger |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=[[Die Presse]] |language=de}}</ref> physicist working in [[Attosecond physics|attosecond science]]. He was a director at the [[Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics]] and a professor of [[experimental physics]] at [[LMU Munich]] in Germany. His research team generated and measured the first [[attosecond]] [[pulse (physics)|light pulse]] and used it for capturing [[electron]]s' motion inside atoms, marking the birth of [[attophysics]].<ref name=":0" /> In 2023, jointly with [[Pierre Agostini]] and [[Anne L'Huillier]], he was awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]]. Since November 2025, he has been Chair Professor at Department of Physics at the [[University of Hong Kong]], [[Pokfulam]], [[Hong Kong]].<ref name=HKU>{{cite news
|title=Nobel Laureate Professor Ferenc Krausz joins HKU as Chair Professor of Physics
|date=17 October 2025
|website=Press Release
|publisher=[[The University of Hong Kong]]
|location=[[Pokfulam]], [[Hong Kong]]
|url=https://hku.hk/press/press-releases/detail/28662.html
}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
From 1981 until 1985 Krausz studied [[theoretical physics]] at [[Eötvös Loránd University]] and [[electrical engineering]] at the [[Technical University of Budapest]] in Hungary.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=מיכל |date=2022-02-08 |title=Ferenc Krausz |url=https://wolffund.org.il/ferenc-krausz/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |website=Wolf Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> From 1987 to 1991 he graduated with a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] at the [[Technical University of Vienna]], in Austria,<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":2" /> and from 1991 to 1993 he also did his [[habilitation]] there.<ref name=":4" /> 1996–1998 he became associate professor,<ref name=":4" /> from 1999 until 2004 professor of electrical engineering at the same institute.<ref name=":4" />

In 2003, he was appointed director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Quantum Optics]] in Garching,<ref name=":3" /> and in 2004 became chair of [[experimental physics]] at [[LMU Munich]].<ref name=":4" />

In November 2025, he was appointed Chair Professor at Department of Physics at the [[University of Hong Kong]], [[Pokfulam]], [[Hong Kong]].<ref name=HKU/>

== Honors and awards ==
* 2006 - [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leibniz Prize |url=https://www.lmu.de/en/about-lmu/lmu-at-a-glance/awards/leibniz-prize/index.html |access-date=2024-01-11 |website=www.lmu.de |language=en}}</ref>
* 2006 – [[Royal Photographic Society]] Progress medal and Honorary Fellowship<ref>{{Cite web |title=Progress Medal |url=https://rps.org/about/awards/history-and-recipients/progress-medal/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |website=Royal Photographic Society |language=en-GB}}</ref>
* 2009 – elected a Fellow of [[Optica (society)|Optica]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 Fellows Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/get_involved/awards_and_honors/fellow_members/elected_fellows/2009_fellows/ |access-date=2023-11-06 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Three Optica Fellows awarded 2023 Nobel Prize in Physics for experimental methods enabling attosecond physics {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/about/newsroom/news_releases/2023/october/three_optica_fellows_awarded_2023_nobel_prize_in_physics_for_experimental_methods_enabling_attosecon/ |access-date=2023-11-06 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>
* 2013 – [[Otto Hahn Prize]]<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Otto Hahn Prize for Ferenc Krausz |url=https://www.mpq.mpg.de/4868153/13_08_092 |access-date=2023-11-21 |website=www.mpq.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref>
* 2015 – selected [[List of Clarivate Citation laureates in Physics|Clarivate Citation laureate in Physics]] with [[Paul Corkum]] "for contributions to the development of attosecond physics."<ref>{{Cite press release |agency=Reuters |title=Thomson Reuters Forecasts Nobel Prize Winners |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/thomson-reuters-forecasts-nobel-prize-winners-300148161.html |access-date=2023-10-04 |website=www.prnewswire.com |language=en}}</ref>
* 2016 – Member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ferenc 2023 -Nobel Prize in Physics Krausz|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/ferenc-krausz/|publisher=German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|access-date=26 May 2021|archive-date=8 March 2022|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220308222059/https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/ferenc-krausz/ |url-status=live}}</ref>
* 2019 – Vladilen Letokhov Medal.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=The first 2019 Vladilen Letokhov Medal goes to Ferenc Krausz|url=https://www.eps.org/blogpost/751263/317740/The-first-2019-Vladilen-Letokhov-Medal-goes-to-Ferenc-Krausz|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220417073238/https://www.eps.org/blogpost/751263/317740/The-first-2019-Vladilen-Letokhov-Medal-goes-to-Ferenc-Krausz|archive-date=17 April 2022|access-date=|website=European Physical Society}}</ref>
* 2022 – [[Wolf Prize in Physics]] with [[Anne L'Huillier]] and Corkum "for pioneering contributions to ultrafast laser science and attosecond physics".<ref name=":4" />
* 2022 – [[BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award]] in Basic Sciences with L'Huillier and Corkum.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-02-22 |title=The Frontiers of Knowledge Award goes to Anne L'Huillier, Paul Corkum and Ferenc Krausz for enabling subatomic particles to be observed in motion over the shortest time scale captured by science |url=https://www.frontiersofknowledgeawards-fbbva.es/noticias/15th-edition-basic-sciences-anne-lhuillier-paul-corkum-ferenc-krausz/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |website=Premios Fronteras |language=en}}</ref>
* 2023 – [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] with L'Huillier and [[Pierre Agostini]] "for experimental methods that generate attosecond pulses of light for the study of electron dynamics in matter."<ref name=":0" />
